name: OpenAI
tagline: Frontier language, image and audio models served via ChatGPT and a developer API.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified. API usage is billed separately by token.

verdictSummary: The product here is not the chat window, it is the model behind it, and the model is the output of a training run that costs more than most countries spend on roads. An agent can absolutely one-shot the wrapper: streaming chat UI, conversation history, system prompts, file attachments, tool calls, all of it in an afternoon. What it cannot do is produce GPT-class weights, or the inference fleet that answers in under a second for hundreds of millions of people. You can self-host a local model and get something genuinely useful for summarizing, drafting and offline work, but on hard reasoning, long context and multimodal input the gap is still obvious. Building the client is the easy part; that is exactly why so many people have already built it.
coreLoopDIY: A local chat app with conversation history, system prompts and streaming responses, pointed at a model running on your own machine via Ollama.
requirements: A machine with enough RAM or VRAM to run a 7B to 70B local model at tolerable speed
Optionally an API key if you want to fall back to a hosted model, which defeats the point
whatYouLose: Frontier reasoning quality: local open weights are good, not GPT-5 good
Very long context windows without your laptop thermal throttling into the sun
Multimodal input and output: voice mode, image generation, video, all gone unless you stitch separate models together
Mobile and desktop apps, sync across devices, shared conversations
Web browsing, code execution sandbox, connectors and the whole tool ecosystem around the chat box
moatNotes: Weights plus a global inference fleet plus a default-choice brand. Any one of those would be hard. All three at once is not a weekend.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because twenty dollars a month for access to one of the best models on earth is, dispassionately, absurd value. Self-hosting a local model is a real and worthwhile thing to do, especially for private data and offline use, but it is a different product with a different quality ceiling. The hardware to run something genuinely competitive costs more than years of subscription, and you still have to maintain it. Most people who build the client end up pointing it at an API key anyway.
notes: The chat UI is a one-sitting build, the thing it talks to is not. The moat is the weights, the compute to make them, and the fleet that serves them at sub-second latency to the whole planet.
prompt:
Build a local-first desktop chat client for self-hosted language models. Empty folder, no accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

Stack, non-negotiable: Vite plus React plus TypeScript, Tailwind for styling, better-sqlite3 for storage, and a tiny Node/Express backend in the same repo. Run the whole thing with one `npm run dev`.

Model backend: talk to a locally running Ollama instance at http://localhost:11434. Read the base URL and default model name from .env (OLLAMA_URL, DEFAULT_MODEL). List available models by calling Ollama's tags endpoint and let the user pick one per conversation.

In scope:
- Streaming responses, token by token, rendered as they arrive.
- Conversation list in a left sidebar: create, rename, delete, search by title and message text.
- Per-conversation system prompt, editable, saved.
- Saved prompt library: named reusable system prompts the user can apply to a new conversation.
- Markdown rendering with syntax-highlighted code blocks and a copy button per block.
- Message editing and regeneration: edit any user message, truncate the thread after it, re-run.
- Token-ish context meter: rough character count against the model's advertised context, with a warning when close.
- Export a conversation as Markdown or JSON.
- Keyboard driven: cmd+k for conversation search, cmd+enter to send, escape to stop generation.
- Stop button that actually aborts the fetch stream.

Out of scope, do not build: user accounts, auth, image generation, voice input, web browsing, tool calling, plugins, RAG over documents, any hosted API fallback.

Store everything in a single data/chat.db SQLite file. Schema with migrations in code, no ORM. Commit a .env.example, never a real .env.

Write a README with setup, the Ollama models you recommend trying, and an honest paragraph on where local models fall short of hosted frontier ones.
